title: First part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. For the first face, draw the first loop consisting of four lines. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0). The second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0438). The third line starts at (0.75, 0.0438) and ends at (0.0, 0.0438). The fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.0438) and returns to the origin (0.0, 0.0). Apply a sketch scale of 0.75 to the first face. Rotate the first face using Euler angles of zero degrees and translate it using a vector of zero. Extrude the first face to a depth of 0.0187 along the normal direction. Ensure no extrusion occurs in the opposite direction of the normal. Define a boolean operation to create a new solid body. The dimensions of the first part are a length of 0.75, a width of 0.04375, and a height of 0.01875. This completes the construction of the first part, which serves as the base of the rectangular bar.

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0438, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0438, 0.0187) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0187) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
